title: BIS applied investigation assessment
scope: Optional, learner-selected practical evidence of evidence and accurate thinking. This supplements the private investigation; it does not assess personality, require disclosure or alter the nine Lab stages or ten learning touchpoints.
sourceBasis: Applied Commerce Competency Framework AC-C03 and progression model APPLY, TEST_AND_REVISE and TRANSFER
BIS canonical Behaviour Contract, Experiment, Evidence Review and Profile architecture
Volume 1 Bis handbooks: field application, adjusting the experiment, mapping a second pattern and identifying what stayed the same or changed
boundary: A learner account stays an account. A facilitator must inspect the shared work and record the basis for verifying practical use. Simulations can demonstrate reasoning under stated conditions, but cannot establish independent real-world action or transfer. No score is a diagnosis, permanent mastery judgement or proof of programme causation.

tasks.title: Use the investigation method
tasks.instruction: Use the method from this Lab in one suitable situation. Save your prediction or plan before the test. Afterwards, show the work, a checkable trace or the action your facilitator can observe. Record what actually happened and what remains uncertain. A situation that did not occur is valid missing opportunity evidence; it is not a failed performance.

criteria.label: The checked work shows the learner using the investigation method in the recorded situation, rather than only saying they intended to use it.

tasks.title: Test and adjust the method
tasks.instruction: Save a prediction or test plan first. Use a suitable opportunity to record what happened. Compare the evidence with the prediction and show a justified adjustment to the method. Keep a missed opportunity, an unchanged result or an unsuccessful attempt visible; none should be replaced by an invented success.

criteria.label: A dated prediction or plan was saved before the observation.
The checked work contains an observation from a suitable opportunity.
The learner compares that observation with the prediction and states limits.
The learner shows a justified adjustment based on that comparison.

tasks.title: Use the method in another context
tasks.instruction: After an earlier application has been reviewed, choose a meaningfully different context. Save the new plan, adapt the method and show distinct work or a checkable trace of its use. Explain what carried over, what changed and what remains uncertain. Naming another context or describing a future intention is not demonstrated transfer.

criteria.label: The checked evidence shows independent use of the method in the new context.
The learner shows and explains the adaptation required in that context.
Distinct earlier reviewed application and later evidence from a different context are both present.
